clue.text: Quarrel with one call centre about room

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: centre asks for the middle letters of the word call

explanation.surface: A row over a call centre seat, with someone demanding more room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'call centre' looks like one phrase; 'centre' picks AL from inside 'call'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spatial is the adjective for things concerning space, so it describes anything to do with room.

clue.text: Unit stops landing spacecraft

indicators.note: stops here means plugs a gap, so the unit sits inside the landing stage

parts.note: a pier is a landing stage for boats
one is a single unit

explanation.surface: A military unit halting a craft as it comes in to land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'landing' reads as touching down, but it is a landing stage, PIER, plugged by ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pioneer was the name of a series of NASA probes launched to explore the outer planets.

clue.text: Doctor runs into milk supplier

indicators.note: into places the runs abbreviation inside the milk supplier

parts.note: a teat delivers milk to the young
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A physician dashing into a dairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb here: to doctor or treat a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor someone is to give them medical treatment, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Clothes soldiers wear are shocking

indicators.note: wear means the shocking word puts the soldiers on, holding them within

parts.note: things that are shocking appal people
RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: A complaint that the uniforms troops wear are appalling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wear' looks like part of the clothing picture but is the container signal; RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a formal word for garments, so it is a synonym of clothes.

clue.text: Ignoring the odds, finches followed calf

indicators.note: dropping the odd-placed letters leaves the even ones of finches followed

explanation.surface: Birds trailing after a young cow, while the odd ones are ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calf' wants to be a young cow; it is a piece of ice broken off a glacier or iceberg.
explanation.definitionFit: A calf is a mass of ice that has broken away from a larger floating sheet or glacier.

clue.text: Actors like empty citadel, not one in Spanish region

parts.note: the actors in a play are its cast

indicators.note: empty means the inside of like is removed, keeping only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Actors fond of a deserted fortress somewhere in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: A second wordplay follows: 'not one in Spanish region' is CASTILE without I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a fortress guarding a city, the same kind of fortified building.

clue.text: He imagines deviant saint breaking abstinence

indicators.note: breaking means splitting the abstinence word open around the other letters

parts.note: a fast is a period of abstinence from food

indicators.note: deviant means going astray, so the letters of saint wander out of order

explanation.surface: A wayward saint interrupting a fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abstinence' suggests the saint's virtue, but it is just a synonym for going without food; 'deviant' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantasist is someone who lives in daydreams, a person who imagines things.

clue.text: It could be nightmarish acting in Morecambe, I gathered

parts.note: an actor on stage is on

indicators.note: gathered means the comic's name takes in the letter I

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was a British comedian, half of the TV double act Morecambe and Wise

explanation.surface: A comic's performance in the seaside town of Morecambe turning into a nightmare.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe is also a Lancashire resort, but here it is the comedian ERIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Oneiric means relating to dreams, and a nightmare is one example of a dream.

clue.text: Perfect spot to welcome new one in home

indicators.note: in places the welcome, new and one pieces within the home word

parts.note: the hearth is the heart of a home
ave is a Latin greeting of welcome
taken as written

explanation.surface: An idyllic place to receive a newcomer at home.
explanation.walkthrough: AVE (hail) is a Latin word of welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes an idyllic place, a paradise found in this life.

clue.text: Extra mushroom, last to be eaten

indicators.note: the final letter of the mushroom is consumed, so it disappears

parts.note: a morel is an edible mushroom

explanation.surface: Asking for more mushroom, saving the last bit for the end of the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last to be eaten' means MOREL loses its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra and further are both ways of saying an additional amount.

clue.text: Each sunflower head in pot is more delightful

indicators.note: in places the each and sunflower pieces within the pot word

parts.note: a planter is a pot for plants

indicators.note: head means the first letter of sunflower

explanation.surface: Every sunflower bloom looks nicer in a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of pleasant means nicer, giving more delight.

clue.text: Workers gather this case of claret in, just about

indicators.note: in places the outer letters of claret within the just about word

parts.note: near means close to, just about

indicators.note: case of means the outside letters of claret, its casing

explanation.surface: Labourers collecting a case of wine, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: The workers are worker bees.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker bees collect the sugary fluid from flowers to make honey.

clue.text: Satirist's rendition of chamber music?

indicators.note: a rendition is a spoken performance, so the phrase is voiced

parts.note: a vault is a chamber and an air is a piece of music

explanation.surface: A satirical writer's version of a chamber music piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chamber music' is not the genre: VAULT (chamber) plus AIR (music), voiced, gives the French writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Voltaire, the French Enlightenment writer, was famous for satires such as Candide.

clue.text: Duke meets crooked alderman in castle in Spain?

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters of alderman are reordered

explanation.surface: A duke encounters a corrupt councillor in a Spanish fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'castle in Spain' is an idiom for a pipe dream, not a building; 'crooked' signals the anagram of alderman.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle in Spain is an idiom for a daydream, a fantasy as unreal as an imaginary world.

clue.text: Each pupil initially put in requests for sweets

indicators.note: put in places the initials inside the requests word

parts.note: someone who requests a job applies for it

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of Each and pupil

explanation.surface: Every pupil first submits applications for sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; 'sweets' means desserts, the British word for a pudding course.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain sweets also means desserts, and fruit pies are a classic dessert.

clue.text: Tweak soft part of foot

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft
a foot is twelve inches

explanation.surface: Massaging the tender part of a sore foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' is the unit of length, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To tweak someone's ear or nose is to nip it between the fingers.

clue.text: Little miner very quiet in bed

indicators.note: in places the quiet marking inside the bed word

parts.note: hay serves as bedding for animals, and to hit the hay is to go to bed
PP, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: A small mine worker lying silently in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The miner is one of the seven dwarfs in Snow White, who work in a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy is one of Snow White's seven dwarfs, small men who mine for gems.

clue.text: Left behind Andrea after surgery on kidney

indicators.note: behind puts the left letter after the rearranged name
after surgery the name has been cut and reshaped, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Andrea recovering after a kidney operation, with something left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after surgery' signals reworked letters; 'on kidney' is a fair definition as the glands sit on top of the kidneys.
explanation.definitionFit: The adrenal glands sit on top of the kidneys, so adrenal describes what lies on the kidney.

clue.text: EU partner ruined entrance

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A European Union partner nation spoils a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' is the verb (en-TRANCE), to delight, not a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to fill them with delight, the same as to enrapture.

clue.text: A Republican poster blocks spies in ideal place

indicators.note: blocks means the poster word sits in the spies word and plugs it

parts.note: the CIA is the American spy agency
an ad, short for advertisement, is a poster

explanation.surface: A Republican's campaign poster obstructs intelligence agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poster' is an advertisement here, and 'blocks' signals one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia is the pastoral paradise of Greek legend, a byword for an idyllic place.

clue.text: Newspaper went for growth in US

parts.note: a rag is slang for a poor-quality newspaper
went, in the childish sense of going to the toilet, can mean weed or urinated

explanation.surface: A newspaper going all out for economic growth in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went' is the colloquial sense of relieving oneself. 'growth in US' is fair because ragweed is a common North American plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragweed is a weedy plant widespread in North America and a notorious cause of hay fever.

clue.text: Impromptu, to pianists, offers 27, 9 or 20

indicators.note: offers means the words present the answer within themselves, held out to the solver

explanation.surface: A piano impromptu is presented to pianists.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references are EDEN, HEAVEN ON EARTH and ARCADIA, all ideal places.
explanation.definitionFit: Each cross-referenced answer names a paradise or perfect place, as does Thomas More's imagined island.

clue.text: Leaves end and start of hole, say

parts.note: on a golf course the green is where a hole ends

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: the tee is where a golf hole begins

explanation.surface: A golfer's description of a hole from its finish to its beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of hole' serves both pieces: the green ends a golf hole and the tee starts it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfermented tea leaves, brewed as a drink, are called by this name.

clue.text: Damn Anglicans coming round for cash

indicators.note: coming round means the Anglicans abbreviation surrounds the damn word

parts.note: CE is the Church of England, the Anglican church
as in I don't give a hang, hang means damn

explanation.surface: Cursed churchgoers being persuaded to part with money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damn' is HANG as in 'hang it!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Change is loose money, coins, so it can stand for cash.

clue.text: 24 hands stuck in plug

indicators.note: stuck in means the hands word is lodged inside the plug word

parts.note: a plug is an advertisement, an ad
hands are workers, men

explanation.surface: Fingers jammed in a plug socket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plug' is a publicity plug, an ad. The cross-reference to 24 brings in the word for alter.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text is to alter it, the verb sense of the cross-referenced answer.

clue.text: Definitive and neat, using Spanish not Latin

indicators.note: using brings in the Spanish abbreviation as a replacement
not drops the Latin abbreviation that the Spanish one replaces

parts.note: a neat spirit is served undiluted
SP is the abbreviation for Spanish

explanation.surface: A tidy and authoritative text in Spanish rather than Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' is not tidy but straight, as a drink. 'using Spanish not Latin' swaps L for SP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something definitive is settled and beyond argument, which is what unquestioned means.

clue.text: English study project in Cornwall garden

parts.note: a den is a private study or retreat

explanation.surface: An English study of a Cornish garden project.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eden Project is a large botanical garden in Cornwall, England; Eden is also the Bible's first garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical paradise garden gives its name to the Cornish garden project under giant biomes.

clue.text: See Welsh girl that's divine

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and a bishop's see
Sian is a Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: Look at the Welsh girl who is heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not look but a bishop's see, here Ely in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Elysian means heavenly, from Elysium, the paradise of Greek myth.

clue.text: Work by 13 John performed with energy

parts.note: john and can are both slang for a toilet
did means carried out or performed
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A writer's work, performed by someone named John with vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' is not a name but slang for a toilet, as is 'can'.
explanation.definitionFit: Candide is Voltaire's satirical novella, the best-known piece by the satirist at 13.
